newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria fin min sees lev/dollar rate at 500 in 97.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria fin min sees lev/dollar rate at 500 in 97.

text.p: Finance Minister Dimitar Kostov said next year's budget assumption for the lev/dollar rate was between 400 and 500.
He declined to give further details on the draft 1997 austerity budget, now being debated by the government.
The lev closed at around 500 to the dollar on Thursday, down from 70 in the beginning of the year.
Kostov said the budget was drafted to accommodate the implementation of a currency board, proposed by the International Monetary Fund (IMF) to restore confidence in the crumbling financial system.

The currency board is a form of fixed exchange rate regime which requires that levs in circulation and commercial banks' mimimum reserves at the central bank match central bank foreign exchange and gold reserves.

Kostov said it was too early to say at what rate the lev will be pegged and to what currency. The dollar is seen as a benchmark of stability, but some circles are lobbying for the mark, as Germany is the biggest investor in the country.

Kostov said parliament should consider collateralising Bulgaria's strategic gold reserves held in the vaults of the central bank, which total some 33 tonnes, or about 1.5 million troy ounces. Part of Bulgaria's gold outside the strategic reserves, amounting to some 4.5 tonnes is deposited abroad.

The Agency for Economic Forecast and Development has said it expects annual interest rates to fall to 30 percent next year after the introduction of a currency board, economic growth is seen at zero in 1997 and annual inflation is seen at between 20 and 30 percent, depending at what rate the lev will be pegged.
